method: Started from the brief's list of well-known 2023-2026 layoffs plus EDGAR submissions and full-text searches for Item 2.05 8-Ks and phrases like 'reduce our workforce' and 'positions' at large companies. Kept a case only if a filing (8-K, often Item 2.05 or the CEO's message as an exhibit, or the 10-K/10-Q) states the count or percentage, and the CEO in office at the announcement has a Summary Compensation Table total for that fiscal year. Pay is the SCT total for the fiscal year in which the cuts were announced; buybacks, dividends and severance are from the same fiscal year's 10-K where it states them in dollars. Every quote was cut verbatim from the cached filing text.

cases.headline: "We've decided to reduce our workforce by approximately 12,000 roles."
cases.notes: Cuts announced in Pichai's January 20, 2023 email, filed as an 8-K. Severance ($2.1 billion) and buybacks ($62.2 billion) are from the 2023 10-K. Pay is the 2024 proxy's Summary Compensation Table; Pichai's 2022 total includes a $218,037,684 stock award, which is why 2022 is far above 2023.

cases.headline: Workforce reductions of approximately 10,000 employees by the end of the third fiscal quarter of 2023
cases.notes: Microsoft's fiscal year ends June 30; the January 2023 cuts fall in fiscal 2023. Cut count from the January 18, 2023 8-K and the fiscal 2023 10-K; severance, buybacks and dividends declared from the 10-K; pay from the October 2023 proxy.

cases.headline: "Overall, we expect to reduce our team size by around 10,000 people"
cases.notes: Zuckerberg's March 14, 2023 post was filed as Exhibit 99.1 to an 8-K; the 2023 10-K confirms approximately 10,000 employees and $1.20 billion of severance. Buybacks ($20.03 billion) include the 1% excise tax accrual. Zuckerberg's salary is $1; nearly all of his reported pay is 'all other compensation', which the proxy says includes about $9.4 million of personal security costs and a $14,000,000 pre-tax allowance for personal security in 2023.

cases.headline: A reduction of the Company's current workforce by approximately 10 percent
cases.notes: Salesforce's fiscal 2023 ended January 31, 2023, so the January 4, 2023 announcement falls in fiscal 2023 (the 10-K says the employee actions were expected to finish in fiscal 2024). The proxy describes Benioff as Chair of the Board and CEO, formerly Co-CEO (with Bret Taylor, formerly Vice Chair and Co-CEO). $683 million is the employee-related part of $828 million of fiscal 2023 restructuring costs.

cases.headline: "Intel expects to reduce headcount by greater than 15% with the majority completed by the end of 2024."
cases.notes: The release says 'greater than 15%'; the 2024 10-K describes an approximate 15% decrease in the core Intel workforce. Intel made no stock repurchases in 2024 (its most recent was in the first quarter of 2021) and suspended its dividend starting Q4 2024, so there is no buyback figure. The 2025 proxy lists Gelsinger as Former CEO.

cases.headline: A restructuring plan that "will impact approximately 5 percent of Cisco's global workforce"
cases.notes: Cisco's fiscal 2024 ended July 27, 2024. Cut share from the February 14, 2024 Item 2.05 8-K; charges, buybacks and dividends from the fiscal 2024 10-K; pay from the October 2024 proxy. A second cut (about 7%) followed in August 2024; see the next case.

cases.headline: A restructuring plan "expected to impact approximately 7 percent of Cisco's global workforce"
cases.notes: Announced August 14, 2024, the first quarter of fiscal 2025 (ended July 26, 2025). The 2025 proxy's table adds a column after Total ('Total as Adjusted for Alternative Stock Award Values', $41,266,351 for fiscal 2025); the figure here is the standard Total column.

cases.headline: "We reduced our operational workforce by approximately 48,000 positions, including 15,000 fewer seasonal positions"
cases.notes: The April 29, 2025 earnings release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) planned approximately 20,000 operational position cuts in 2025; the 2025 10-K reports the actual reduction of approximately 48,000 positions, including 15,000 fewer seasonal positions. Buybacks and dividends from the 2025 10-K; pay from the 2026 proxy.

cases.headline: "We plan to reduce the size of our total workforce by roughly 10 percent"

Starbucks made no share repurchases in fiscal 2025, so the $2.8 billion returned to shareholders was dividends. Niccol joined in September 2024; his fiscal 2024 total ($95,801,676) includes $90,291,772 of stock awards.

rejected.name: Amazon (Andy Jassy), 2023 and 2025 corporate cuts
rejected.reason: No SEC filing states a role count or percentage: the 10-Q/10-K report only estimated severance ($470 million in Q1 2023; $2.7 billion in 2025 'primarily related to planned role eliminations'). The 18,000 and 14,000 figures came from blog posts that were not filed. Amazon also made no buybacks in 2023-2025.

rejected.name: Tesla (Elon Musk), April 2024 cut of more than 10%
rejected.reason: Musk's 2024 Summary Compensation Table row is all dashes, so there is no printed CEO pay figure for the year of the cuts.

rejected.name: Disney (Bob Iger), 7,000 jobs in 2023
rejected.reason: The 7,000 figure was given on the earnings call; neither the 8-K release, the 10-Qs nor the fiscal 2023 10-K state a job count (only severance charges).

rejected.name: Nike (John Donahoe), February 2024 cut of about 2%
rejected.reason: The December 2023 Item 2.05 8-K and fiscal 2024 10-K describe only 'a net reduction of our global workforce' and $400-450 million of charges, with no count or percentage.

rejected.name: PayPal (Alex Chriss), January 2024 cut of about 2,500 roles
rejected.reason: The 2024 10-K describes a 'global workforce reduction' with $307 million of charges but gives no count or percentage; no Item 2.05 8-K was filed.

rejected.name: Chevron (Mike Wirth), 2025 plan to cut 15-20% of workforce
rejected.reason: The 10-Ks describe $2-3 billion of structural cost reductions and severance accruals but never state the percentage or a headcount.

rejected.name: Citigroup (Jane Fraser), 20,000 roles
rejected.reason: Full-text search found no 10-K, 10-Q or 8-K with the 20,000 figure; the 10-K mentions restructuring charges and 'significant reductions in functional roles' only.

rejected.name: Target, October 2025 corporate cuts (about 1,800 roles)
rejected.reason: No filing found with the role count.

rejected.name: CVS Health, 2023 corporate workforce cuts
rejected.reason: The 10-Q reports $344 million of severance for 'corporate workforce optimization' but no count.

rejected.name: Walgreens Boots Alliance, October 2024 plan
rejected.reason: The Item 2.05 8-K counts store closures (about 1,200-1,300), not jobs; it says most store workers would be redeployed.

rejected.name: HP Inc., November 2025 plan (4,000-6,000 employees)
rejected.reason: Falls in fiscal 2026, whose CEO pay has not been disclosed yet; the earlier 4,000-6,000 plan was announced in November 2022.

rejected.name: Microsoft 2025 cuts (about 15,000 in May and July 2025)
rejected.reason: The fiscal 2025 10-K gives no job count; only the January 2023 cut has a filed number (included).

rejected.name: Accenture, March 2023 (about 19,000 people)
rejected.reason: The 10-Q states the number, but Accenture plc is incorporated in Ireland; left out to keep the set to US companies.

rejected.name: Dell Technologies, February 2023 (about 5%)
rejected.reason: Confirmed in an Item 2.05 8-K, but left out: the announcement came three days into fiscal 2024 while the charges went into fiscal 2023, so the pay year is ambiguous; Michael Dell's Summary Compensation Table total was $2,797,308 for fiscal 2023.
